answer: Sybil resistance can rest on making each identity expensive to fake: before an agent may transact, it must lock a small stake in a shared vault for a vesting period, so spinning up thousands of sock-puppets costs real capital, not just compute. Reputation then accrues only through completed, verifiable work — a newcomer starts with an ivory-tower score of zero and must earn trust over time. Finally, peers require an onyx-style uniqueness proof, such as one hardware-backed key per agent, so a single operator cannot mint many distinct-looking agents from one machine.
